requestedActions.title: List active task titles with pagination

guide.summary: Register one OAuth app, request only data:read, and have a test account authorize it. Then call GET /api/v1/tasks to list task titles. Pagination and the active-only filter are not fully documented for this endpoint, so verify them during the first call. Avoid write-capable scopes. Production review, distribution to other workspaces and token exchange details remain unknown.

findings.title: OAuth authorization URL is documented
findings.detail: Users are redirected to Todoist's authorization endpoint with client_id, scope, state and response_type=code. Redirect URIs are configured in the App Management Console.

evidence.quote: https://app.todoist.com/oauth/authorize?client_id = 0123456789abcdef & scope = data:read,data:delete & state = secretstring & response_type = code
Redirect users to the authorization URL at the endpoint
This JSON error will be returned to the requester (your user's browser) if redirect URI is not configured in the App Management Console.

findings.title: Request data:read for task listing
findings.detail: data:read is documented as read-only access that includes tasks. It is the mapped grant for listing task titles.

evidence.quote: data:read Grants read-only access to application data, including tasks, projects, labels, and filters.

findings.title: Do not request write-capable scopes
findings.detail: data:read_write adds write access to tasks and must not be requested for this read-only use case. Task creation, update, completion and deletion are excluded.

evidence.quote: data:read_write Grants read and write access to application data, including tasks, projects, labels, and filters. This scope includes task:add and data:read scopes.

findings.title: Redirect URI must be configured before consent
findings.detail: If the redirect URI is not configured in the App Management Console, the authorization request fails with a JSON error. Configure it before the first authorization test.

evidence.quote: Redirect URI Not Configured
This JSON error will be returned to the requester (your user's browser) if redirect URI is not configured in the App Management Console.

steps.title: Register the OAuth app and configure the redirect URI
steps.detail: In the App Management Console, create the app and set the redirect URI used by the callback. Record client ID and client secret in your secret store. Done when the app shows a client ID and the redirect URI is saved.
steps.doneWhen: App exists in the console with client ID and a saved redirect URI.

evidence.quote: This JSON error will be returned to the requester (your user's browser) if redirect URI is not configured in the App Management Console.
When the user denies your authorization request, Todoist will redirect the user to the configured redirect URI with the error parameter: http://example.com?error=access_denied .

steps.title: Build the authorization URL and callback with data:read only
steps.detail: Build the authorization redirect with response_type=code, scope=data:read and a random state value. Build a callback that handles the error parameter. Code-to-token exchange is not documented in the supplied sources, so keep it unimplemented until verified. Done when the URL contains only data:read.
steps.doneWhen: Authorization URL built and checked to contain scope data:read and no write scope.

evidence.quote: https://app.todoist.com/oauth/authorize?client_id = 0123456789abcdef & scope = data:read,data:delete & state = secretstring & response_type = code
data:read Grants read-only access to application data, including tasks, projects, labels, and filters.
When the user denies your authorization request, Todoist will redirect the user to the configured redirect URI with the error parameter: http://example.com?error=access_denied .

steps.title: Authorize the individual test account
steps.detail: Use a representative test Todoist account, not a shared admin account. Open the authorization URL, approve the consent screen and confirm it shows read-only access. Done when the callback receives a code or access_denied is handled.
steps.doneWhen: Test account grants consent and the callback receives a code.

evidence.quote: https://app.todoist.com/oauth/authorize?client_id = 0123456789abcdef & scope = data:read,data:delete & state = secretstring & response_type = code
When the user denies your authorization request, Todoist will redirect the user to the configured redirect URI with the error parameter: http://example.com?error=access_denied .

steps.title: Call GET /api/v1/tasks and list task titles
steps.detail: Use the access token from the test account to request tasks, then extract content for each task. Pagination parameters are not documented in the supplied sources, so check the response for pagination fields and make a second request only if one is present. Expected response: a JSON object with a results array of tasks. Boundary check: confirm the call is a GET with no body and that the response contains titles without any write being made.
steps.doneWhen: Task titles are returned from the test account and pagination fields are recorded.

evidence.quote: get /api/v1/tasks https://api.todoist.com /api/v1/tasks
Response samples 200 Content type application/json

steps.title: Verify granted access and absence of write calls
steps.detail: Check the consent screen and the granted scope for data:read only. Review the outgoing request log to confirm only GET calls were made. Boundary check: no POST, PATCH, DELETE or task-completion requests appear in the log.
steps.doneWhen: Granted scope is data:read only and the request log shows only GET requests.

evidence.quote: data:read Grants read-only access to application data, including tasks, projects, labels, and filters.
data:read_write Grants read and write access to application data, including tasks, projects, labels, and filters. This scope includes task:add and data:read scopes.
